analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md. The only changed ranges are lines 404-410 (load-eviction text) and 1050-1070 (segmented paged KV admission). The rest of the units are unchanged context. No source code was supplied, so I examined documentation claims only.

The changed text makes these claims:
- Free 64 MiB KV segments are parked per pool, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8).
- Parked segments sit outside the grant, floor and ledger charge.
- The next same-size admission reinstalls them.
- New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages.
- Parked backing is dropped on refused admission, on a process-wide release request (memory pressure, refused charge, load gate, preload check) and after 30 s idle.
- Load eviction first calls releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, and pre-accept counts retained segments as reachable.
- DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 are the rollbacks.

Relevant threats:
- T-028 (residual KV/GPU data) and TB-007: parked segments are reused across requests without a documented scrub. The provider operator is already an adversary with memory access, and prior KV content is not exposed to consumers by this description. I see no new consumer-facing disclosure. Whether reinstalled segments are overwritten before any read depends on unseen code.
- T-010/T-029 (availability): up to 2 GiB per pool of uncharged memory could cause memory overcommit if the release triggers fail. This is an accounting assumption that cannot be verified from the documentation. The doc lists several release paths, and the ledger and floor do not count the parked bytes.
- T-041 (prefix cache): this change does not touch SSD cache identity, TTL, HMAC naming or DBK3 crypto, so the at-rest posture is unchanged.

No security regression is supported by the supplied evidence. The next pass should check PagedKVSegments.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift and KVPoolReclaimer to confirm that:
- reinstalled parked segments cannot be read before being written, and are scoped per pool/model;
- the uncharged parked bytes are released before any admission, load or memory-pressure decision that assumes they are free;
- the load-gate behavior (releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad) cannot free memory still owned by in-flight work.
